prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি (language bn).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ফসল" · longest unbreakable word 69px · one-line width 149px
  col 2: header "বপন" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 263px
  col 3: header "কাটা" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 239px
  col 4: header "ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 108px
  col 5: header "মন্তব্য" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 1035px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare crops by their sowing and harvest windows, yield index, and accompanying notes in a seasonal schedule.","reading":"Row by row: identify the crop in column 1, compare the paired sowing and harvest timing in columns 2–3, read the yield in column 4, then consult the comment in column 5.","groups":["Columns 2 and 3 form a paired sowing–harvest timeline and should have similar widths so the two dates can be compared across rows.","Column 4 is a compact numeric attribute attached to the timing pair and needs much less width than the date columns.","Column 1 is the row identifier and should stay strong; column 5 is secondary commentary whose width depends on whether notes or schedule comparison is prioritized."],"keep_intact":["Crop names and variety identifiers such as বোরো ধান (উফশী), আমন ধান (স্থানীয়), গম (বারি গম-৩৩), সরিষা (বারি সরিষা-১৪)","Numeric yield values and the unit টন/হেক্টর","Month names and date words, which may wrap at spaces but must not break mid-word"],"may_wrap":["Sowing and harvest date ranges in columns 2–3 at natural word spaces","Long comments in column 5","Longer crop names only at spaces or parentheses if the crop column is tightened"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[170,150,145,85,169],"idea":"Row-first balance: keep crop names intact, give the paired timing columns nearly equal moderate widths, and leave the remainder for readable notes."},{"name":"B","widths":[140,175,170,80,154],"idea":"Schedule-comparison priority: widen the sowing and harvest columns for easier cross-row timing comparison, accepting some crop-name wrapping and a narrower notes column."},{"name":"C","widths":[170,120,115,75,239],"idea":"Notes-led layout: preserve full crop names and give comments substantial space, while compressing the timing columns into compact multi-line date blocks."}]}
